summary: Agent passed all baseline tests but missed four integrity edge cases in the new test suite.

details.reasoning: The implementation is substantial and passes all 42 baseline tests, but four of 143 maintenance tests fail. It rejects a store folder reached through a symlink because ensureFolder uses NOFOLLOW_LINKS; properties inherited through Properties.defaults are not detected when rejecting default.fileNames alongside a constructor strategy; shared entries whose names resolve to the same file outside the folder are classified as broken before the shared override is applied; and an invalid index name causes InvalidPathException to escape instead of being reported as a broken entry. These are implementation omissions in explicitly specified integrity behavior.
details.secondary_factors: The agent changed only production code and documentation; no test manipulation or external execution failure was observed.

justification.issue_description: Several explicitly required integrity cases are not implemented: shared status must take precedence over broken status, malformed names must be reportable as broken entries, constructor strategies must reject configured fileNames including inherited Properties defaults, and a store folder reached through a link must work.
justification.evidence: The prompt says that entries resolving to one file are shared and that an entry both shared and something else stays shared; it requires configuring default.fileNames for a constructor-strategy store to be rejected; and it requires broken entries to be reported and repaired. The failing implementation uses properties.containsKey at TextFileBasedViolationStore.java:137, rejects symlink folders at :285-287, requires direct paths before assigning identities at :613-620, and calls Path.resolve without handling InvalidPathException at :784-785. JUnit reports the four corresponding failures, while junit_base.xml reports 42/42 passing.
justification.verdict_reasoning: FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is appropriate because the code runs and implements most of the requested feature, but it does not satisfy several clear requirements and foreseeable integrity edge cases. This is not a test or environment mismatch: the failures reach the changed production code and the reference design handles these cases by following folder links, checking effective configuration, classifying shared entries before broken entries, and catching invalid paths.

quick_failure_summary: Four integrity edge cases fail: symlinked folders, inherited fileNames configuration, shared entries reaching an outside file, and malformed index names.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is broad but detailed and solvable. The tests exercise deterministic filesystem and concurrency scenarios, and the reference implementation confirms feasibility.

evidence: junit_base.xml reports 42 tests, 0 failures, and 0 errors; the baseline Gradle run is successful.
junit_new.xml reports 143 tests, 4 failures, and 0 errors, with stack traces in TextFileBasedViolationStore rather than bootstrap or dependency failures.
test_execution.log reports wrapper exit code 1 solely because the new suite is 139/143, and the agent changed only TextFileBasedViolationStore.java and documentation.
trajectory.json contains no observed runtime, dependency, permission, or verifier failure; its final note only says formatting download was unavailable and does not show material diversion.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external environment or verifier blocker was found; the failing behavior is attributable to the implementation.
